locator: §19, first paragraph; compare §18, second paragraph and §20, first paragraph
interpretation: §18: the council, following Vatican I, teaches that Jesus Christ built the holy Church, 'missis Apostolis sicut Ipse missus erat a Patre' (John 20.21). §19: the Lord Jesus constituted the twelve 'ad modum collegii seu coetus stabilis', sent them 'ut suae participes potestatis' to make all peoples disciples, to sanctify and to govern them (citing Matthew 28.16-20 and John 20.21-23), 'sicque Ecclesiam propagarent'; the apostles by preaching gather the universal Church 'quam Dominus in Apostolis condidit' and built on Peter. §20: that divine mission, entrusted by Christ to the apostles, lasts to the end of the age; the bishops who succeed them are 'doctrinae magistri'. Read as a conciliar assertion that the founding of the Church was done through the apostles' sending, in Christ's own mission from the Father and with a share in his power that includes discipling (teaching). Limits: it is a doctrinal assertion, not historical corroboration; the council's 'Ecclesia' is read as the Church of §8, which subsists in the Catholic Church, and that identification is the content of stage 6, not of this claim; the source speaks of the Father, not of an arbitrary mandator; it does not state that every society Jesus founded is this Church. It supports, and does not state, STMT-MANDATE-COVERS-JESUS-FOUNDING-OF-CATHOLIC-CHURCH.
